note: Svarog is the father of Veles (reconstructed genealogy).
explanation: This father-son relationship is a scholarly reconstruction (Ivanov & Toporov), not a single attested myth [S6].

note: Perun and Veles are the great antagonists (the sky-thunder-god vs. the underworld-serpent-god).
explanation: The 'Perun-Veles' conflict is a scholarly reconstruction (Ivanov & Toporov), not a single attested myth [S6].

note: Perun and Veles are in conflict (the sky-thunder vs. the underworld-serpent).
Jarilo (spring/youth) and Morana (winter/death) are the great antagonists of the seasonal cycle.
explanation: The seasonal Jarilo-Morana opposition is a scholarly reconstruction from folk ritual [S6].

note: Jarilo and Morana are in opposition (the spring vs. the winter).
Nebo (the sky-father) and Perun (the thunder-god) are both 'sky' deities; their relationship is debated.
explanation: Whether Nebo is the supreme god above Perun, or a folk Christianization that absorbed Perun's role, is debated [S6].

note: Perun and Dazhbog are both members of the Kiev pantheon (the 'sky/sun' group).
explanation: Both are named in the Kiev idol list; their exact relationship is not specified [S1][S2].

note: Perun and Khors are both members of the Kiev pantheon.
Perun and Stribog are both members of the Kiev pantheon.
(Variant) In some reconstructions Perun and Veles are siblings; in others Veles is Svarog's son.
explanation: The relationship between Perun and Veles is not consistent: some see them as siblings, others as Veles being Svarog's son [S6].

note: (Reconstructed) Mokosh is sometimes seen as Perun's consort (the earth-mother to the sky-father).
explanation: The Perun-Mokosh pairing is a reconstructed parallel to the Indo-European sky-father/earth-mother, not a single attested myth [S6].

note: Svarog (the forge-fire) and Perun (the sacred fire) are both 'fire' deities; their relationship is debated.
explanation: The 'sacred fire' is attributed to both Svarog and Perun in different sources; the relationship is debated [S4][S6].

note: Dazhbog and Khors are both solar/light deities; their distinction is not clear.
explanation: Both are named in the Kiev idol list as solar/light deities; their distinction is not well-defined [S4].

note: The Zorya (the dawn) is associated with Nebo (the sky) — the 'gate' of the sky.
Veles (the underworld-god) is associated with Cherd (the lord of the underworld).
explanation: Both are 'underworld' deities; their exact relationship is not attested [S6].

note: (Reconstructed) Morana (death) is associated with Cherd (the underworld).
